title: Verify a new anonymous seeker can complete the guided questionnaire with all preference fields answered
description: This test case validates the primary happy path for a new, anonymous user. It ensures that a user can successfully provide answers to all preference questions in the guided questionnaire, submit them, and have their data captured by the system. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a first-time visitor, I want to fill out the entire job preference questionnaire so the platform can understand my needs and show me relevant job listings, demonstrating its value before I need to create an account.
prerequisites:
1. User is a new visitor with no existing session cookies or account for the platform.
2. The guided questionnaire feature is enabled on the home page.
3. The backend services for preference capture and job matching are available.
stepsToPerform:
1. Clear all browser cookies and local storage for the application domain.
2. Navigate to the application's home page.
3. Observe that the guided questionnaire is presented to the user.
4. For 'working arrangement', select 'Fully Remote'.
5. For 'motivation', select 'Career Progression'.
6. For 'target annual salary', enter '95000'.
7. For 'location', select 'United States'.
8. For 'job titles', enter 'Product Manager'.
9. For 'years of experience', select '5-7 years'.
10. For 'highest level of education', select 'Bachelor's Degree'.
11. Complete all other available preference fields with valid data.
12. Click the 'Submit' or 'Find Jobs' button to complete the questionnaire.
expectedResult:
1. The system accepts all the provided preference data without errors.
2. The user is redirected to a personalized job results page.
3. The job listings displayed are filtered and ranked according to the preferences submitted.
4. The user is not prompted to create an account or pay to see the results.

sourceCitation.location: L21-L25, Functional Requirements: 1. SEEKER PREFERENCE CAPTURE
sourceCitation.excerpt: Collect the seeker's requirements through a short guided questionnaire offered from the home page on a first visit, before any account exists.

title: Verify the system records which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered when a seeker skips questions
description: This test ensures the system correctly handles partial questionnaire submissions. It verifies that both answered and unanswered questions are recorded, and that job matching proceeds using only the data the user provided.
testDescription: As a new visitor who may not have all the answers or is in a hurry, I want to be able to skip some questions in the preference questionnaire and still get relevant job matches based on the information I did provide.
prerequisites:
1. User is a new visitor with no existing session cookies or account.
2. The questionnaire allows for optional fields or a 'skip' option.
3. The backend can distinguish between a null/skipped value and a provided value.
stepsToPerform:
1. Clear all browser cookies and local storage for the application domain.
2. Navigate to the application's home page.
3. Begin the guided questionnaire.
4. For 'job titles', enter 'Data Analyst'.
5. For 'location', select 'Canada'.
6. For 'target annual salary', leave the field blank or explicitly click 'Skip'.
7. For 'highest level of education', leave the field blank or explicitly click 'Skip'.
8. Complete a few other preference fields but ensure at least two are left unanswered.
9. Click the 'Submit' or 'Find Jobs' button to complete the questionnaire.
10. Observe the job results page and the active filters displayed.
11. (If available) Navigate to a preference summary/edit page.
expectedResult:
1. The system successfully processes the partially completed questionnaire.
2. The job results are filtered based on the provided preferences ('Data Analyst', 'Canada').
3. The skipped preferences (salary, education) do not act as filters on the results.
4. The system's internal session data for the user correctly reflects that the salary and education preferences were left unanswered.

sourceCitation.location: L36-L40, Functional Requirements: 1. SEEKER PREFERENCE CAPTURE
sourceCitation.excerpt: Record which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered.

title: Verify a seeker can add job titles up to the defined maximum limit
description: This is a boundary value analysis test to confirm that the system correctly enforces the upper limit for the number of job titles a seeker can target. It tests the 'max' boundary condition. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a job seeker with a diverse skill set, I want to be able to enter multiple target job titles, up to the maximum allowed, to ensure I see a wide range of relevant opportunities.
prerequisites:
1. The maximum number of target job titles is defined and configured in the system (ASSUMPTION: max limit is 5).
2. User is a new visitor on the home page with the questionnaire active.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the home page and start the guided questionnaire.
2. Proceed to the step for entering target job titles.
3. Enter the first job title: 'Senior Project Manager'. Observe it is accepted.
4. Enter the second job title: 'Program Manager'. Observe it is accepted.
5. Enter the third job title: 'Scrum Master'. Observe it is accepted.
6. Enter the fourth job title: 'Agile Coach'. Observe it is accepted.
7. Enter the fifth job title: 'Product Owner'. Observe it is accepted.
8. Verify that all 5 job titles are displayed correctly in the UI.
9. Submit the questionnaire.
expectedResult:
1. The system accepts all 5 job titles without error.
2. The UI correctly displays the 5 added titles.
3. Upon submission, all 5 titles are saved to the seeker's preference profile and used for job matching.

title: Verify a seeker is prevented from adding job titles beyond the defined maximum limit
description: This is a negative boundary test (max+1) to ensure the system prevents users from exceeding the defined limit for target job titles. It protects data integrity and user experience. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a user, I expect the system to provide clear limits and feedback. If I try to enter more job titles than are allowed, I want the system to stop me and explain the rule, rather than failing silently or producing an error.
prerequisites:
1. The maximum number of target job titles is defined and configured in the system (ASSUMPTION: max limit is 5).
2. User is a new visitor on the home page with the questionnaire active.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the home page and start the guided questionnaire.
2. Proceed to the step for entering target job titles.
3. Enter the first job title: 'Software Engineer'.
4. Enter the second job title: 'Backend Developer'.
5. Enter the third job title: 'Cloud Engineer'.
6. Enter the fourth job title: 'DevOps Engineer'.
7. Enter the fifth job title: 'Solutions Architect'.
8. Verify that all 5 job titles have been added successfully.

expectedResult:

title: Verify a seeker can revisit and change their preferences after initial submission without repeating the whole questionnaire
description: This test verifies that a user can easily modify their saved preferences after the initial onboarding. This is crucial for user experience, allowing them to refine their search without starting from scratch.
testDescription: As a job seeker, my priorities might change or I might want to refine my search after seeing initial results. I want to be able to easily edit my preferences, like my target salary, without having to go through the entire multi-step questionnaire again.
prerequisites:
1. An anonymous seeker has already completed the questionnaire in their current session.
2. The user is on the job results page.
3. A UI element (e.g., 'Edit Preferences', 'Filters' button) exists to modify preferences.
stepsToPerform:
1. As a new user, complete the guided questionnaire with a target salary of '$80,000'.
2. Submit the questionnaire and land on the job results page.
3. Observe the jobs returned, which are matched against the '$80,000' salary.
4. Locate and click the 'Edit Preferences' or similar link/button.
5. Observe a view that displays the current preferences without restarting the questionnaire flow.
6. Change the target salary from '$80,000' to '$110,000'.
7. Save the changes.
8. Observe the job results page refreshes or updates.
expectedResult:
1. The user is presented with an interface to edit individual preferences, not the full questionnaire.
2. The change to the target salary is successfully saved.
3. The job results list updates to reflect the new salary preference, showing different or re-ranked listings.
4. Other, unchanged preferences remain in effect.

title: Verify the guided questionnaire is offered from the home page for a first visit before any account exists
description: This test validates the primary entry point for the preference capture workflow. It ensures that a genuinely new visitor, with no prior history, is correctly identified and prompted to start the questionnaire.
testDescription: As a new visitor landing on the platform's home page for the first time, I expect to be guided on how to get the most value. The platform should proactively ask for my job preferences to help me get started.
prerequisites:

expectedResult:

title: Verify a seeker can successfully upload a resume in a common document format that is under the defined size limit
description: This test validates the happy path for the resume upload feature. It ensures that standard, valid files are accepted and processed correctly by the system. Automation: HIGH (requires a mock file upload service).
testDescription: As a job seeker, I want to upload my resume in a standard format like PDF or DOCX so that it can be stored with my profile and used for job matching and future applications.
prerequisites:
1. The system is configured to accept specific file formats (e.g., PDF, DOCX).
2. A maximum file size is defined (ASSUMPTION: 5MB).
3. A test resume file exists in a supported format (e.g., 'test_resume.pdf') and is under the size limit (e.g., 1MB).
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the home page and start the guided questionnaire.
2. Proceed to the resume handling step.
3. Select the option indicating the resume is 'up to date'.
4. Click the 'Upload Resume' button.
5. In the file selection dialog, choose the valid test file ('test_resume.pdf', 1MB).
6. Confirm the selection and initiate the upload.
7. Observe the UI for feedback during and after the upload process.
expectedResult:
1. The file upload process completes successfully without any errors.
2. The UI displays a confirmation message, such as 'test_resume.pdf uploaded successfully'.
3. The system associates the uploaded document with the current anonymous user's session.

title: Verify the system confirms that an uploaded document has been received before it is treated as part of the seeker's profile
description: This test focuses on the user feedback and state management aspect of resume uploads. It ensures the system provides explicit confirmation of receipt and only then integrates the resume into the user's profile.
testDescription: As a user, when I upload an important document like my resume, I need clear confirmation that the system has received it successfully. I want to be sure it's saved before I move on.
prerequisites:
1. An anonymous seeker is in the process of completing the questionnaire.
2. A valid resume file ('my_cv.docx', < 5MB) is available for upload.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the resume upload step within the questionnaire.
2. Click the 'Upload Resume' button and select the valid file 'my_cv.docx'.
3. Initiate the upload.
4. Observe the UI immediately after the upload completes for a confirmation message.
5. After seeing the confirmation, complete the rest of the questionnaire and submit.
6. Navigate to the job results page.
7. If a 'My Profile' or 'My Documents' link is available, click it to view the session summary.
expectedResult:
1. A clear and unambiguous success message (e.g., 'Upload complete', 'my_cv.docx has been received') is displayed in the UI.
2. The UI state changes to reflect the presence of an uploaded resume (e.g., showing the filename and an option to replace or delete it).
3. The resume is now considered part of the seeker's profile for the remainder of the session and will be used in matching.

title: Verify the system rejects a resume upload in an unsupported format with a clear reason
description: This is a negative test using equivalence partitioning to ensure the system's file type validation is working correctly. It verifies that unsupported file formats are rejected and that the user receives helpful feedback.
testDescription: As a user, if I accidentally try to upload the wrong type of file (e.g., an image instead of a document), I expect the system to prevent the upload and tell me what file types are acceptable, so I can correct my mistake.
prerequisites:
1. The system is configured to reject certain file extensions (e.g., .png, .txt, .exe).

title: Verify a seeker can select the current state of their resume as 'up to date', 'needs work', or 'not written yet'
description: This test verifies that the system correctly presents and captures the seeker's self-reported resume status. This data is important for understanding user segments and tailoring the user experience. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: As an anonymous job seeker, I want to indicate the current status of my resume during the onboarding process so the platform understands my level of job search readiness. I should be able to choose between 'up to date', 'needs work', or 'not written yet'.
prerequisites: The user is a new, anonymous visitor with no existing session data. The guided questionnaire is enabled and accessible from the home page.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the FlexJobs home page.
2. Start the guided questionnaire.
3. Proceed through the questionnaire to the 'Resume Handling' section.
4. Observe the three radio buttons or selectable options for resume status: 'up to date', 'needs work', and 'not written yet'.
5. Select the 'up to date' option and verify it becomes highlighted/selected.
6. Select the 'needs work' option and verify the selection changes from 'up to date' to 'needs work'.
7. Select the 'not written yet' option and verify the selection changes again.
8. Proceed to the next step in the questionnaire to ensure the value is submitted.
9. (Verification) Inspect the session data via developer tools or test hooks to confirm the value 'not written yet' is stored.
expectedResult:
1. The user can select any one of the three provided resume status options.
2. Only one option can be selected at a time; selecting a new option deselects the previous one.
3. The system correctly records the final selected status against the anonymous seeker's session profile.

title: Verify an uploaded resume is retained against the seeker for use in matching during an anonymous visit
description: This test ensures that a resume uploaded during an anonymous session is persisted and actively used by the matching engine to personalize job results. This is a core part of demonstrating platform value prior to registration. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: As an anonymous job seeker, after I upload my resume, I expect the system to analyze its contents and use that information to show me more relevant jobs, even if the keywords are not in the preferences I selected manually.
prerequisites: The user is an anonymous seeker. A test resume file ('resume_python_aws.docx') is available, containing specific keywords like 'Python Developer' and 'AWS'. The job database contains listings that match these keywords.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the FlexJobs home page as a new anonymous user.
2. Start the guided questionnaire.
3. Enter preferences that are intentionally different from the resume content (e.g., Job Title: 'Marketing Manager').
4. In the 'Resume Handling' section, select the option to upload a resume.
5. Upload the test resume 'resume_python_aws.docx'.
6. Confirm the resume upload was successful.
7. Complete the questionnaire and navigate to the job results page.
8. Analyze the matched job listings displayed.
9. Verify that jobs matching the resume keywords (e.g., 'Senior Python Developer') are present in the results.
expectedResult:
1. The uploaded resume is successfully associated with the anonymous user's session.
2. The job matching algorithm uses the content of the uploaded resume to influence the filtered and ranked job listings.
3. Job listings relevant to the resume's content (e.g., 'Python Developer' roles) are displayed to the user, demonstrating the resume was processed for matching.

sourceCitation.location: L51-L55, Functional Requirements: 2. RESUME HANDLING

title: Verify the seeker can widen an individual preference from the results page and see the listings update
description: This test verifies the dynamic 'widen' filter functionality on the results page, which allows users to iteratively refine their search without re-doing the entire questionnaire. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: As a job seeker viewing my search results, if I feel the criteria are too restrictive, I want to be able to widen a specific filter (like salary) and see the list of jobs update immediately with more options.
prerequisites: The user has completed the questionnaire with a specific preference (e.g., Target Salary: '$120,000'). The user is currently on the job results page viewing the initial, filtered list of jobs.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, complete the questionnaire with a target salary of '$120,000'.
2. Submit the questionnaire and land on the job results page.
3. Note the total number of job listings found (e.g., '45 results').
4. Locate the 'Salary' filter control on the results page.
5. Interact with the control to widen the preference (e.g., change the minimum salary to '$100,000').
6. Observe the job listings section of the page for a refresh.
7. Verify that the list of jobs automatically updates.
8. Check the new total number of job listings displayed.
expectedResult:
1. The job listings update immediately after the preference is widened.
2. The new total number of results is greater than the original count (e.g., more than 45).
3. The newly included jobs match the widened criteria (e.g., jobs with salaries between $100,000 and $120,000 now appear).

sourceCitation.location: L56-L60, Functional Requirements: 3. JOB MATCHING AND RESULTS

title: Verify the system indicates which constraint is narrowing the set when a combination of preferences returns very few listings
description: This test ensures the system provides helpful feedback when a search is too specific, guiding the user on how to widen it to see more results. This improves user experience and prevents abandonment. Automation feasibility: MEDIUM.
testDescription: As a job seeker, if my combination of preferences is so specific that it returns almost no jobs, I want the system to tell me which of my choices is the most limiting factor so I can easily adjust it and see more results.
prerequisites: The job database is populated such that a specific combination of filters will yield very few results (e.g., < 5). The threshold for 'very few' is defined. Test combination: Job Title: 'Lead Lunar Geologist', Location: 'Antarctica'.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, navigate to the home page and start the questionnaire.
2. Enter a common preference, e.g., Salary: '>$80,000'.
3. Enter a very restrictive preference, e.g., Location: 'Antarctica'.
4. Enter a second very restrictive preference, e.g., Job Title: 'Lead Lunar Geologist'.
5. Submit the questionnaire and navigate to the results page.
6. Observe that very few (or zero) results are returned.
7. Look for a specific UI message or indicator on the page designed to provide feedback.
8. Verify the message identifies either 'Location: Antarctica' or 'Job Title: Lead Lunar Geologist' as a limiting constraint.
expectedResult:
1. A user-friendly message is displayed when the number of results is below the defined threshold.
2. The message explicitly names the preference that is causing the low result count (e.g., 'Few results for your selected Location. Try widening this preference.').
3. The system correctly identifies one of the most restrictive filters.

sourceCitation.location: L61-L65, Functional Requirements: 3. JOB MATCHING AND RESULTS

title: Verify captured preferences are applied to subsequent searches for the remainder of the anonymous visit
description: This test verifies that preferences are persistent within a single anonymous session, ensuring a consistent user experience as they navigate the site without forcing them to re-enter criteria. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: As an anonymous job seeker, after I complete the questionnaire once, I expect my preferences to be remembered for my entire visit. If I navigate to other pages and then come back to the job search, my filters should still be active.
prerequisites: The user is an anonymous visitor with no existing session cookies for the site.
stepsToPerform:
1. In a new incognito browser session, navigate to the FlexJobs home page.
2. Complete the questionnaire with specific preferences (e.g., Working Arrangement: 'hybrid', Job Category: 'Finance').
3. Submit the questionnaire and view the personalized job results.
4. Verify the results match the 'hybrid' and 'Finance' criteria.
5. Navigate away from the results page to a non-search page, like the 'About Us' or 'Blog' page.
6. Use the main site navigation to return to the primary job listings page.
7. Observe the active filters displayed on the job listings page.
8. Verify that the 'hybrid' and 'Finance' preferences are still active and applied to the search results without any further user input.
expectedResult:
1. Preferences captured from the initial questionnaire are stored in the user's session.
2. When the user performs a new search or returns to the job listings page during the same visit, the previously captured preferences are automatically applied.
3. The user is not prompted to complete the questionnaire again during the same session.

title: Verify an anonymous seeker can browse listings, complete the questionnaire, and view matched results without an account or payment
description: This test verifies the core value proposition: a user can get personalized results before being asked to register or pay. This is critical for user acquisition and demonstrating platform value. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: As a first-time visitor, I want to explore the platform's job listings and see how well it matches my needs before I commit to creating an account. I should be able to complete the preference survey and see personalized results without any gates.
prerequisites: The user is a new, anonymous visitor with no account. The browser session is clean (no cookies, not logged in).
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a new incognito/private browser window.
2. Navigate to the FlexJobs home page.
3. Verify that no login wall, registration form, or payment prompt is presented.
4. Click the button to start the guided questionnaire.
5. Proceed through all steps of the questionnaire, providing valid preferences.
6. Submit the questionnaire.
7. Verify that the job results page loads with a list of matched jobs.
8. Click on one of the job listings in the results.
9. Verify the job detail page is displayed with full information.
10. Throughout this entire flow, confirm that at no point was the user required to create an account or provide payment details.

title: Verify registration is requested when an anonymous seeker acts on a listing by applying
description: This test verifies the correct state transition from an anonymous user to a registration-prompted user when attempting to apply for a job. This confirms that the value-first approach (show jobs before signup) is correctly implemented, gating high-intent actions behind registration.
testDescription: As an anonymous visitor who has found an interesting job, I want to click the 'Apply' button. I expect the system to then ask me to create an account or log in before I can proceed with the application.
prerequisites: The user is in an anonymous session (starting state). A list of matched jobs is displayed on the results page. The user does not have an existing account.
stepsToPerform:
1. Start on the home page as an anonymous user.
2. Complete the preference questionnaire to generate job listings.
3. On the results page, identify a job listing of interest.
4. Click the 'Apply' button associated with that listing (the action).
5. Observe the resulting UI change.
6. The system should display a modal, overlay, or redirect to a page prompting the user to register or sign in.
7. Verify that the user is not taken to an external application site directly.
8. Verify that the original job listing context is maintained (e.g., the registration form mentions the job being applied for).
expectedResult:
1. The system successfully intercepts the 'Apply' action.
2. A registration/login prompt is displayed to the user.
3. The user's state transitions from 'anonymous browsing' to 'registration required'.
4. The application process is blocked until registration or login is completed.

title: Verify all preferences captured before registration carry over into the new account when the seeker signs up
description: This test verifies the integrity of user preference data during the critical state transition from an anonymous session to a registered user account. It ensures a seamless user experience where no data is lost upon sign-up.
testDescription: A new, anonymous visitor completes the onboarding questionnaire to set their job preferences. When they decide to register an account by acting on a job listing, all previously selected preferences should be automatically saved to their new profile without requiring re-entry.
prerequisites: User must have a clean browser session (no existing cookies or logged-in state). The platform has job listings available that will trigger a registration prompt when acted upon (e.g., saving).
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, navigate to the application's home page.
2. Observe and begin the guided questionnaire.
3. Select a specific set of preferences: Working Arrangement='fully remote', Motivation='income', Target Salary='150000', Location='Germany'.
4. Submit the questionnaire and land on the job results page. Verify the results are filtered.
5. Locate a job listing in the results and click the 'Save' button.
6. Observe the registration modal or page is displayed as expected.
7. Complete the registration form using a unique email address (e.g., test+pref-carryover@example.com) and a secure password.
8. Submit the registration and get logged into the new account.
9. Navigate to the 'My Profile' or 'My Preferences' section of the account.
10. Verify that the preferences for Working Arrangement, Motivation, Salary, and Location match exactly what was entered in step 3.
expectedResult:
1. The newly created user account contains the exact preferences set during the anonymous session.
2. The user is not prompted to complete the questionnaire again after registration.
3. The data is persisted correctly and is visible in the user's account settings.

title: Verify uploaded documents and personal details are handled in line with applicable data protection obligations
description: This test performs a basic check to ensure that sensitive user data is handled with fundamental security measures, such as encrypted transmission. This is a baseline requirement for protecting user privacy and complying with data protection regulations. Automation: Medium.
testDescription: A user provides personal information during registration and uploads a resume. This test verifies that all communication with the server containing this sensitive data is encrypted using HTTPS, and that sensitive data like passwords are not exposed in the UI.
prerequisites: Access to browser developer tools (Network tab). The application is hosted on a secure server with a valid SSL/TLS certificate.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the application's registration page.
2. Open the browser's developer tools and select the 'Network' tab.
3. Fill in the registration form with test data, including an email and password.
4. Submit the registration form.
5. In the Network tab, inspect the request sent to the server. Verify the URL begins with 'https://'.
6. Proceed to the resume upload step.
7. Upload a test document.
8. Inspect the network request for the file upload and verify its URL also begins with 'https://'.
9. Log in and navigate to the account settings page where the user's email is displayed.
10. Navigate to any 'Change Password' form and verify the current password field is masked (e.g., shows dots instead of characters).
expectedResult:
1. All form submissions containing personal data (registration, login) are sent over a secure HTTPS connection.
2. All document uploads are sent over a secure HTTPS connection.
3. Sensitive data such as passwords are always masked in the user interface.
